flags: minor: cricket-chirp temperature context is a familiar SAT/textbook trope; not a close mirror of a specific released item as far as I can tell
Q055-01.notes: 14 s = 14/60 min, so n = c*14/60 = 7c/30; T = 7c/30 + 40. B is the inverted conversion trap; C ignores the 60; D adds 40 before converting.

Q055-02.notes: Gap 9 mi, closing speed 6 mph. First 2 mi apart after closing 7 mi (70 min); second time after passing, closing 11 mi: 11/6 h = 110 min. Positions at 110 min (7.58, 5.58) stay on the trail. Trap answer 70.

Q055-03.notes: Break-even 315/(4-1.5)=126, then 315/(5-1.5)=90; decrease 36. D=90 is the new break-even (trap); C=315/5; A=315/20.

Q055-05.notes: d/(s-c) + d/(s+c) = 2ds/(s^2-c^2). B ignores the current (common trap); C has the sign error; D swaps s and c in the numerator.

Q055-06.notes: The minimum 3 occurs at x=2, so f=a(x-2)^2+3. f(0)=4a+3=7 gives a=1, and f(5)=9+3=12.

Q055-07.notes: Substitute y=12-x: xy+4x = 16x - x^2, which has its maximum at x=8, giving 64. A graphing calculator makes this routine.

Q055-08.notes: 40*sqrt(t)=160, so sqrt(t)=4 and t=16. B=4 forgets to square; D=(260/40)^2 forgets to subtract 100; A=sqrt(4).

Q055-09.notes: 40/36 h = 66 min 40 s; minus 2 min 40 s = 64 min; 40/(64/60) = 37.5 km/h. The speeds are realistic for a time trial.

Q055-11.notes: Area = 4*pi = 12.57 m^2; 0.45/12.57 = 0.0358 m/min, about 3.6 cm/min. A uses the diameter as the radius (0.9); C divides by 2*pi (7.2); D omits pi (11.25).

Q055-12.notes: Overhang (70-40)/2 = 15; height = sqrt(25^2-15^2) = 20. Area (40+70)/2*20 = 1100 cm^2, times 300 cm = 330,000 cm^3 = 330 L. Dimensions are realistic.
